source.name: beyond-all-reason/spring (Recoil engine)
source.status: registered historical upstream release source; no runtime selection claim

components.title: Released command and queue observation route
components.summary: The released engine submits normal AI commands, exposes team-owned command queues, and provides separate Lua views of rally and factory production queues.

components.title: Released sequential factory edit route
components.summary: Factory count options and insert/remove operations mutate queues through ordinary per-command paths; array submission loops over commands.

flows.title: AI submission and bounded queue observation candidates

steps.description: Validates actor ownership and sends one AI command through the synchronized network protocol.
For a factory, selects newUnitCommands, which is the rally queue for newly produced units.
Selects the factory commandQue, which is the production queue.
Calls the Lua message handler through an explicitly unsynced AI call-in and returns an optional string.

flows.title: Ordinary factory count and queue edit behavior

steps.description: Maps option zero to one item, SHIFT to a factor of five and CONTROL to a factor of twenty.
Adds or removes the computed number of production entries using ordinary queue mutations.
Parses an array and calls GiveCommand once per command.
Removes matching commands by tag or ID with iterative queue edits.

facts.statement: At the exact released source revision, GetUnitCommands selects a factory newUnitCommands queue while GetFactoryCommands selects commandQue, providing distinct rally and production observation domains. A bounded team-scoped Lua bridge is therefore a source-supported observation route.
RecvSkirmishAIMessage is explicitly always unsynced, so it can carry a bounded observation request and response but is not a synchronized mutation or transaction boundary.

GiveOrderArrayToUnit loops through commands and invokes GiveCommand separately; the inspected released path contains no rollback around the loop. It cannot establish all-or-none nonempty queue replacement.
Factory production uses a count multiplier of one by default, five for SHIFT and twenty for CONTROL, then appends or removes that many ordinary queue entries.

The released source supports useful-play commands and truthful later queue observation, but these paths do not prove the later strict cancellation/refund, synchronized fence, dedupe, rollback, or independent peer-service contract.

open_questions: Which exact engine artifact is selected and loaded by the next native game process?
Will a packaged bounded Lua observation bridge pass real native perspective, completeness, framing and freshness checks?
Does the product retain strict all-or-none replacement as mandatory, or select the stock-compatible useful-play profile?
